title: Choice-word certificates for a decided language
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $a,c$ be natural numbers. Suppose that on every input $x$, every choice word of length $a\cdot 2^{|x|^c}$ makes $N$ halt, and that $x\in L$ if and only if some such choice word makes $N$ halt with output exactly $1$. Then, for every binary string $x$, $x\in L$ if and only if there is a binary string $u$ of length $a\cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ such that $xu$ belongs to the choice-word verifier language for $N,a,c$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine deciding a language $L$ within time $a \cdot 2^{n^c}$ on inputs of length $n$. For every binary string $x$: $x \in L$ if and only if there is a string $u$ with $|u| = a \cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ such that $x\,u$ lies in the exponential choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $a, c$.
